The foundational theorem establishes that any measure μ on a σ-ring S can be completed to a larger σ-ring S* such that all subsets of measure-zero sets in S are included. This process avoids reliance on outer measure theory. The proof hinges on showing that the class S of sets of the form E Δ N, where E ∈ S and N ⊂ A with μ(A) = 0, forms a σ-ring. Symmetric difference closure implies countable union closure, thus forming a σ-ring. The resulting measure μ* on S* satisfies μ*(E Δ N) = μ(E), ensuring completeness. This construction allows for consistent extension of measurable domains without introducing external measure-theoretic constructs.
